WYRMWOOD RESERVE — Eighteen pine martens have been released into the Wyrmwood reserve, marking the return of the species to the area, people familiar with the matter said.

The first release took place on 14 October 2023. The animals, 11 females and 7 males, were set free across three sites within the reserve.

Dr. Elspeth Harrowgate, Lead Conservation Biologist for the Wyrmwood Reserve Trust, oversaw the operation, the people said.

The reintroduction follows the Wyrmwood Reintroduction Feasibility Report (2022), which was approved by the Trust's Board of Governors. The document set out the case for bringing the pine marten back to the reserve.

The Trust has not detailed what monitoring will follow the releases. Those familiar with the matter said the three-site approach was intended to spread the founding animals across the reserve.

Meridian Brief will update this item as further details emerge.
